mcp_server/magic.tagline: Generate React UI components by describing them
mcp_server/magic.overview: Magic generates React UI components on demand from a plain-language description. It drops the generated components straight into popular IDEs, so you can build interfaces by saying what you want instead of writing them by hand. It is a fast way to scaffold UI while you code.
capabilities: Generate React UI components on demand
useCases: Students building a React project who want components quickly
Developers prototyping a UI and wanting starter components in their IDE
howTo: Visit 21st.dev/magic and follow the setup for your IDE
Register the Magic MCP server with your IDE or MCP client
Describe the React component you want
Review the generated component and place it in your project

example.label: Prompt example
example.code: Create a responsive pricing card component in React with a title, price, and call-to-action button

goodToKnow: Output is React components, so it fits React/JSX projects best.
Check generated code before shipping; AI-generated UI still needs review.

mcp_server/computer-control.tagline: Automate mouse, keyboard, and screen actions
mcp_server/computer-control.overview: Computer Control MCP automates desktop actions for an AI agent. It can move the mouse and keyboard, take screenshots, recognize on-screen text, and manage windows. This lets an agent operate apps the way a person would, by clicking and typing.
useCases: Students automating repetitive desktop tasks
Anyone scripting an agent to operate apps that lack an API
howTo: Run npx -y computer-control-mcp to start the server
Register it with your MCP client
Grant any OS permissions needed for screen and input control
Ask the agent to click, type, screenshot, or manage windows
goodToKnow: Controlling your mouse and keyboard can have real effects, so supervise what it does.
May require operating-system permissions for screen capture and input control.

mcp_server/knowledge-graph-memory.overview: Knowledge Graph Memory is an official reference MCP server that stores facts as a knowledge graph of entities, relations, and observations. This lets an AI assistant remember details about you and your projects and recall them across separate conversations, instead of forgetting everything between sessions. It is a simple, local persistent memory layer.
capabilities: Stores facts as entities connected by relations
Adds observations to entities over time
Recalls remembered information in later conversations
Lets the assistant search and read its own memory graph
Persists the graph locally as a JSON file
useCases: Keeping an assistant aware of your preferences and ongoing projects
Building a personal assistant that remembers people and context
Maintaining continuity across many short chat sessions
howTo: Add the memory server to your MCP client config
Run it with npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-memory
Optionally set MEMORY_FILE_PATH to choose where the graph is stored
Tell the assistant to remember a fact, then start a new chat and ask about it
Inspect the JSON memory file to see what was stored
goodToKnow: Memory is only as good as what the assistant chooses to write; results vary by client.
The graph is stored in plain text locally, so treat it as you would any local data file.

mcp_server/shodan.tagline: Query Shodan and CVE data for device intel
mcp_server/shodan.overview: Shodan MCP queries the Shodan API and the CVE database. It returns data about internet-connected devices and details on known vulnerabilities. It is useful for security research and looking up exposure or vulnerability information.
useCases: Security students researching exposed devices and CVEs
Researchers checking vulnerability details from chat
howTo: Run npx -y @burtthecoder/mcp-shodan to start the server
Provide your Shodan API key
Register the server with your MCP client
Ask it about devices or CVE details
goodToKnow: Requires a Shodan API key.
Use the data responsibly and only for legitimate research.

mcp_server/web-fetch.tagline: Fetch pages as Markdown with image extraction
mcp_server/web-fetch.overview: Web Fetch fetches web pages and converts them to Markdown. It extracts images and supports proxies, so you get clean, readable page content. It is useful when you want a page turned into tidy Markdown for notes or further processing.
useCases: Students turning articles into Markdown notes
Anyone feeding clean Markdown page content into a workflow
howTo: Run npx -y @kwp-lab/mcp-fetch to start the server
Register it with your MCP client
Optionally configure a proxy if needed
Ask it to fetch a page and return Markdown
goodToKnow: This is a small community project (very low star count), so expect basic features.
Conversion quality can vary depending on the page's structure.

mcp_server/read-mysql.tagline: Read-only MySQL query access for analysis
mcp_server/read-mysql.overview: This server gives read-only query access to MySQL databases. You can join tables and analyze your data without making any changes, which keeps it safe for exploration and reporting.
capabilities: Makes no changes to the database
useCases: Students querying a MySQL database for analysis without risk of edits
Anyone who wants safe, read-only reporting access through their assistant
howTo: Run npx -y @benborla29/mcp-server-mysql to start the server
Provide your MySQL connection details
Register the server with your AI client
Ask your assistant to query and join tables for analysis
goodToKnow: Access is read-only, so it won't modify your data.
You still need valid credentials for the MySQL database you want to read.

mcp_server/maigret-osint.tagline: Find a username across social networks
mcp_server/maigret-osint.overview: This server runs Maigret OSINT to find a username's accounts across many social networks. It is built for open-source intelligence gathering, helping you see where a given username appears online.
capabilities: Searches for a username across social networks
Finds accounts tied to a username
useCases: Researchers checking where a username appears across social platforms
Anyone doing open-source intelligence on a public username
howTo: Run npx -y mcp-maigret to start the server
Register the server with your AI client
Give your assistant a username to look up
Review the accounts Maigret finds across networks
goodToKnow: Use it only on public information and in line with applicable laws and policies.
It builds on the Maigret OSINT tool for its searches.

mcp_server/searxng-meta-search.tagline: Private web search via your own SearXNG
mcp_server/searxng-meta-search.overview: This server runs privacy-focused web searches through a self-hosted SearXNG instance. It returns aggregated results from many engines without tracking you.
useCases: A student who wants private search results in their AI workflow
Someone running their own SearXNG who wants to query it from chat
howTo: Run npx -y @kevinwatt/mcp-server-searxng to start the server
Point it at your self-hosted SearXNG instance
Add the server to your MCP client config
Ask your AI client to search the web
goodToKnow: You need a self-hosted SearXNG instance to point it at.
Privacy depends on how your SearXNG instance is configured.

mcp_server/llama-cpp-bridge.tagline: Bridge MCP clients to a local llama.cpp server
mcp_server/llama-cpp-bridge.overview: This server connects MCP clients to a local llama-server instance running llama.cpp. It supports chat completions and health checks so you can use a locally hosted model from your AI client.
capabilities: Connect MCP clients to a local llama-server
useCases: A student running a local LLM and wanting to call it from their client
Someone keeping inference offline with llama.cpp
howTo: Start a local llama-server with llama.cpp
Run npx -y @openconstruct/llama-mcp-server to start the bridge
Add the bridge to your MCP client config
Send chat completion requests to your local model
goodToKnow: You need a running local llama-server (llama.cpp) for it to bridge to.
Health checks help confirm the local server is reachable.

mcp_server/counsel.overview: This server connects to the Counsel API for strategic reasoning. It runs multi-perspective analysis and structured AI debate on a question to help you think it through.
capabilities: Hold structured AI debate on a question
useCases: A student weighing different sides of a decision
Someone wanting structured pros-and-cons reasoning on a tough question
howTo: Get the server from github.com/mercurialsolo/counsel-mcp
Build and add it to your MCP client config with Counsel API access
Ask your AI client to run a multi-perspective analysis or debate
Review the perspectives it returns

example.label: Example prompt
example.code: Debate whether I should self-host or use a managed database.

goodToKnow: Requires access to the Counsel API.
Output is reasoning and debate, not a single definitive answer.

mcp_server/applescript.tagline: Let AI use Mac apps via AppleScript
mcp_server/applescript.overview: This MCP server runs AppleScript on macOS, giving your AI assistant access to apps like Notes, Calendar, Contacts, Messages, and Finder. It lets your assistant automate everyday Mac apps.
useCases: A student automating Mac tasks like creating notes or calendar events
Anyone who wants AI to reach native Mac apps through AppleScript
howTo: Install and run the server with: npx -y @peakmojo/applescript-mcp
Grant the macOS automation permissions it requests
Add the server to your MCP client's configuration
Restart your client and ask it to use a Mac app
goodToKnow: This is macOS-only and needs automation permissions for the apps it controls.
Since it can act in apps like Messages, review actions before they run.

mcp_server/kagi-search.tagline: Kagi web search and page summaries
mcp_server/kagi-search.overview: Kagi Search adds Kagi's web search and AI summarization to your AI tools. It returns fast search results and can summarize the contents of pages.
capabilities: Add current-info lookup to AI tools
useCases: A student doing research who wants quick search results and summaries
Someone who prefers Kagi as their search engine inside their assistant
howTo: Get a Kagi account and API access (kagi.com)
Add the Kagi MCP server to your AI client config with your key
Ask your assistant to search the web or summarize a page
Read the results and summaries
goodToKnow: Kagi is a paid search service, so you'll need an account.
Summaries are AI-generated and worth double-checking for key facts.

mcp_server/llm-code-context.tagline: Pick the right files for code review
mcp_server/llm-code-context.overview: LLM Code Context helps with code review and documentation by selecting the relevant files and outlining code across many languages. It gives your AI assistant the right slice of a codebase to work with.
capabilities: Select relevant files from a codebase
useCases: A student preparing context for an AI to review their project
A developer who wants to share just the relevant code with an assistant
howTo: Run npx -y llm-context to start the server
Add it to your MCP client config
Ask your assistant to select and outline relevant files
Use the context for review or documentation
goodToKnow: Works across multiple languages for file selection and outlining.
Designed to feed context to an assistant rather than edit code itself.

mcp_server/epicshop-workshop.tagline: AI instructor for Epic Web workshops
mcp_server/epicshop-workshop.overview: EpicShop Workshop is an AI instructor for Epic Web workshop repos like EpicReact.dev and EpicWeb.dev. It gives you fast, contextual help as you work through the exercises.
capabilities: Guide you through Epic Web workshop exercises
Answer questions about the workshop material
useCases: A student working through an EpicReact or EpicWeb workshop
A learner who wants hints without leaving their workshop repo
howTo: Run npx -y @epic-web/workshop-mcp to start the server
Add it to your MCP client config
Open your Epic Web workshop repo and ask your assistant for help
Follow the guidance as you do the exercises
goodToKnow: Designed specifically for Epic Web workshop repositories.
Most useful while actively working through the exercises.

mcp_server/svelte-docs.overview: Svelte Docs lets your AI assistant query the official Svelte and SvelteKit documentation. It pulls framework-specific reference and examples right into your chat.
useCases: A student learning Svelte who wants accurate doc-based answers
A developer checking SvelteKit reference without leaving their assistant
howTo: Run npx -y mcp-svelte-docs to start the server
Add it to your MCP client config
Ask your assistant a Svelte or SvelteKit question
Read the doc-grounded answer and examples
goodToKnow: Answers are grounded in the official Svelte documentation.

mcp_server/crowdstrike-falcon.overview: CrowdStrike Falcon connects your AI assistant to the CrowdStrike Falcon security platform so it can query detections, incidents, and threat intelligence. Security data becomes accessible from chat.
useCases: A security student or analyst exploring Falcon data
An SOC team member querying detections from their assistant
howTo: Run npx -y falcon-mcp to start the server
Add it to your MCP client config with your CrowdStrike API credentials
Ask your assistant about detections or incidents
Review the returned security data
goodToKnow: Requires a CrowdStrike Falcon account and API access.
Built by CrowdStrike for querying their security platform.

mcp_server/deepl-translator.overview: DeepL Translator translates and rephrases text between languages using the DeepL API, with control over formality. You can translate from your AI assistant in plain language.
useCases: A student translating study material or messages
Someone who wants high-quality translations with formality control
howTo: Run npx -y deepl-mcp-server to start the server
Add it to your MCP client config with your DeepL API key
Ask your assistant to translate or rephrase text
Read the translated result
goodToKnow: Requires a DeepL API key.
Formality control depends on the languages DeepL supports for it.

mcp_server/netlify.tagline: Manage Netlify deploys in plain language
mcp_server/netlify.overview: The Netlify MCP server manages Netlify projects and deployments through natural-language commands. It can automate site setup and publishing so you do not have to click through dashboards. This makes shipping a site as simple as describing what you want.
useCases: A developer who wants to deploy a site without leaving their AI assistant
A student learning web hosting who prefers plain-language commands

Authenticate with your Netlify account
Add the server to your MCP client configuration
Ask your AI assistant to set up or publish a site

Deployment actions affect live sites, so review requests carefully

mcp_server/vibe-composer-midi.tagline: Turn prompts into music in real time
mcp_server/vibe-composer-midi.overview: Vibe Composer MIDI composes and plays music from natural-language prompts in real time. It offers 128 MIDI instruments and tempo control, so you can describe the music you want and hear it played back.
capabilities: Play the music in real time
useCases: Music students who want to sketch ideas by describing them in plain language
Hobbyists experimenting with melodies and instruments without a DAW
howTo: Install the server by running npx -y vibe-composer-midi-mcp
Add it to your MCP client configuration
Restart the client to load the server
Describe the music you want and let the assistant compose and play it
goodToKnow: It works with MIDI instruments and tempo control, so output is MIDI-based rather than recorded audio.

mcp_server/elasticsearch.overview: This Elasticsearch server lets an AI assistant search and manage Elasticsearch indices using plain language instead of hand-written queries. You can describe what you are looking for and let the assistant handle the query.
capabilities: Use plain language instead of raw queries
Let an assistant translate requests into searches
useCases: Developers who want to query Elasticsearch without writing query DSL
Teams managing indices who want assistant help with search and upkeep
howTo: Install the server by running npx -y @awesome-ai/elasticsearch-mcp
Provide your Elasticsearch connection details
Add it to your MCP client config and restart it
Describe a search in plain language and let the assistant run it
goodToKnow: You will need access to a running Elasticsearch instance for it to connect to.

mcp_server/gis-data-conversion.overview: GIS Data Conversion converts geographic data between formats like WKT, GeoJSON, CSV, TopoJSON, and KML, and also offers reverse geocoding. An AI assistant can use it to reshape map data or turn coordinates into place information.
capabilities: Convert between WKT, GeoJSON, CSV, TopoJSON, and KML
Help an assistant handle GIS data
useCases: Students working with maps who need to convert geographic file formats
Developers handling GIS data who want quick format conversion and reverse geocoding
howTo: Install the server by running npx -y gis-dataconversion-mcp
Add it to your MCP client configuration
Restart the client so the server loads
Ask the assistant to convert a GIS file or reverse geocode coordinates
goodToKnow: It handles the listed geographic formats; other formats may not be supported.

mcp_server/lenny-s-podcast.overview: Lenny's Podcast server runs full-text search over transcripts of Lenny's Podcast. An AI assistant can use it to find discussions of topics like pricing and growth across episodes.
capabilities: Surface episodes covering things like pricing and growth
Help an assistant pull relevant quotes
useCases: Founders and product people researching pricing, growth, and related topics
Students looking for expert discussion on product and startup themes
howTo: Clone or install the server from its GitHub repository (github.com/akshayvkt/lenny-mcp)
Follow the repository's setup instructions
Add the server to your MCP client config
Restart the client and ask the assistant to search the transcripts
goodToKnow: It searches transcripts of Lenny's Podcast specifically, not other shows.
No one-line install command is listed, so follow the repository's setup steps.

mcp_server/alteryx-server.overview: Alteryx Server is an MCP server that connects to Alteryx Server to automate data workflows. It can manage users and track jobs as part of analytics processes. This suits people who use Alteryx for data preparation and want an assistant to help run it.
useCases: Data analysts who run Alteryx workflows and want assistant-driven automation
Teams managing Alteryx users and monitoring job runs
howTo: Run the server with npx -y mcp-server-alteryx
Provide your Alteryx Server URL and credentials
Connect it to your MCP-compatible AI client
Ask the assistant to run a workflow or check a job
goodToKnow: You need access to an Alteryx Server installation with valid credentials.
It is a community wrapper, so confirm it fits your Alteryx version.

mcp_server/mirror.overview: Mirror is an MCP server that prompts self-reflection and introspective questioning. It uses MCP sampling and configurable prompts to ask thoughtful questions. This is for people who want an assistant to help them reflect rather than just answer tasks.
useCases: Students journaling or reflecting on their learning
Anyone who wants guided introspective prompts from an assistant
howTo: Run the server with npx -y mirror-mcp
Configure the prompts you want it to use
Connect it to your MCP-compatible AI client
Ask the assistant to start a reflection session
goodToKnow: It relies on MCP sampling, so your client must support that feature.
It is a small, experimental community project.

mcp_server/web-ui-copy.tagline: Save a web page as offline, script-free HTML
mcp_server/web-ui-copy.overview: Web UI Copy is an MCP server that turns a web page into standalone, script-free HTML. It inlines resources as base64 so the page can be analyzed offline. This is useful when you want a clean, self-contained copy of a page to study.
capabilities: Convert a web page to standalone HTML
useCases: Developers who want a clean offline copy of a page's UI
Students analyzing a web page's layout without running its scripts
howTo: Run the server with npx -y mcp-copy-web-ui
Connect it to your MCP-compatible AI client
Give it the URL of the page you want to copy
Ask the assistant to save the page as offline HTML
goodToKnow: Scripts are stripped, so interactive parts of the page will not work.
Inlining resources can make the saved HTML file large.

mcp_server/vmware-fusion.overview: VMware Fusion is an MCP server that controls VMware Fusion virtual machines through its REST API. It handles power state, lifecycle, and status of VMs. This is useful for people who run virtual machines and want assistant control.
useCases: Developers running VMware Fusion VMs through an assistant
Anyone starting, stopping, or checking VMs without the GUI
howTo: Run the server with npx -y vmware-fusion-mcp-server
Enable the VMware Fusion REST API and provide credentials
Connect it to your MCP-compatible AI client
Ask the assistant to start or check a VM
goodToKnow: You need VMware Fusion installed with its REST API enabled.
It controls VM power and lifecycle, so use it carefully.

mcp_server/pubmed-research.tagline: Search PubMed papers and build citations
mcp_server/pubmed-research.overview: This MCP server lets an AI assistant search PubMed for biomedical papers and pull back abstracts and metadata. It can also generate citations and track how many times papers have been cited. It is handy for literature reviews and staying grounded in real published research.
useCases: A student writing a biology or medical paper who needs sourced references
A researcher doing a literature review and tracking a paper's impact
howTo: Run the server with npx -y scholarly-research-mcp
Add the server to your MCP client configuration
Ask your assistant to search PubMed for a topic
Request abstracts, metadata, or a formatted citation

This is a small community project (around 13 GitHub stars)

A student building a dataset of faces for a machine learning experiment
howTo: Run the server with npx -y @dasheck0/face-generator
Add the server to your MCP client configuration
Ask your assistant to generate one or a batch of faces
Save the generated images to your dataset folder

useCases: A tech lead planning a weekly learning hour for their engineering team
A coach designing hands-on practice grounded in the team's real code activity

Provide GitHub access so it can analyze activity

Ask your assistant to generate a learning hour session

useCases: A student generating a presentation from an outline
A professional quickly assembling and exporting a deck to PDF

Add the server to your MCP client configuration

Export the finished deck to PDF

This is a small community project (around 5 GitHub stars)

mcp_server/higress-ai-search.tagline: Add real-time web search to AI answers
mcp_server/higress-ai-search.overview: This MCP server adds real-time web search results to AI responses through the Higress gateway. It can pull results from engines like Bing so answers reflect current information. It helps ground your assistant's replies in fresh web data.
capabilities: Add real-time web search to responses
useCases: A developer wanting an assistant that pulls in up-to-date web results
A student researching current topics that need fresh information

Ask your assistant a question that needs current web results

This is a small community project (around 5 GitHub stars)

mcp_server/youtube-subtitles.tagline: Fetch YouTube transcripts by natural language
mcp_server/youtube-subtitles.overview: This MCP server retrieves and transcribes YouTube subtitles. It lets you fetch a video's transcript through natural language queries in your AI assistant. It is a quick way to get the text of a video without watching it.
useCases: A student pulling a lecture video's transcript to study or search it
A creator grabbing a video's text for notes or summaries

Register the server in your MCP client config
Ask your assistant for a YouTube video's transcript by URL
Read or summarize the returned subtitles

mcp_server/gotify-notifications.tagline: Send push notifications to your Gotify server
mcp_server/gotify-notifications.overview: This MCP server sends push notifications with custom titles and messages to your own Gotify server. It is configured through environment variables. It lets an AI assistant alert you through self-hosted notifications.

Register the server in your MCP client config
Ask your assistant to send a notification with a title and message

mcp_server/harvest.tagline: Track time in Harvest with plain language
mcp_server/harvest.overview: This MCP server lets you track time, projects, and hours in Harvest using plain-language commands instead of the app's interface. It connects your AI assistant to your Harvest account. It makes logging and reviewing time faster through chat.

A team member reviewing time and projects quickly

Ask your assistant to log or review time
